successors.name: Aceh Sultanate
successors.text: Aru: the east coast of Sumatra from the Deli hinterland to Asahan and Labuhan Batu, the land Iskandar Muda conquered in 1613 (the same expression the sultanate-of-aceh dossier uses); the page links…

successors.name: deli
successors.text: Deli, founded in 1632 when Gocah Pahlawan was appointed 'to rule the former territory of Aru'

ledger.x: c. 1539: Aceh probably takes the port city of Kota Rentang. 'Probably 1539: Aceh likely took the port city of Kota Rentang' and 'under Aceh pressure' the capital moved inland to Benteng Putri Hijau; the sultanate-of-aceh dossier's 1539 gain is the Batak country, not the port, so the counterpart is read from this page…

c. 1540: the capital moves inland from Kota Rentang to Benteng Putri Hijau (Deli Tua). The page dates it to the 'early 16th century' under Aceh pressure; 1540 follows the probable loss of the port in 1539.
1564: Aru is defeated in the Ottoman expedition to Aceh.
1564: the Ottoman-backed campaign is closed in the year it opens.

wars.name: Aceh's conquest of Aru
wars.outcome: Aceh probably took Kota Rentang in 1539 and Iskandar Muda 'struck a final blow' in 1613; Aru was dissolved in the early 17th century.

wars.name: Majapahit expedition to Haru and Pane
wars.outcome: 'A Majapahit naval expedition gained control of Haru and Pane' in 1339; the Nagarakretagama of 1365 lists Aru as a Majapahit vassal in Sumatra.

certainty.note: The kingdom's site is argued (Medan, Belawan, Wampu, Barumun); the shape is the land Aceh took in 1613.
